claims.text: High hardness and strength in HEAs are primarily governed by large lattice distortions.
Configurational disorder produces large lattice distortions in HEAs.
Lattice distortions act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Dislocation pinning by lattice distortions impedes dislocation motion and increases strength and hardness through solid-solution strengthening.
Configurational disorder and its associated lattice distortions enhance work hardening.
Minor secondary-phase precipitation or compositional gradients can reduce configurational disorder.
Local compositional fluctuations act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Secondary-phase formation or compositional segregation reduces lattice distortions and their dislocation-pinning effect.
Reducing lattice-distortion-mediated pinning decreases strength and hardness.
A fully disordered, single-phase HEA will have higher hardness and yield strength than samples with introduced ordering or secondary phases.
A lower density of dislocation-pinning centers produces more mobile dislocations and lower mechanical resistance.
Matching grain size and processing conditions is sufficient to isolate the effect of lattice distortion in the proposed comparison.
The hypothesis is intended to hold only while the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution.
Extensive phase separation or brittle intermetallic formation may cause mechanisms other than lattice-distortion strengthening to dominate.
The quantitative relationship between lattice distortion and mechanical properties can vary with alloy composition and processing history.
Comparable or greater hardness and yield strength in the reduced-disorder samples relative to the baseline would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is bounded to alloys that remain single-phase, but the proposed modified comparison deliberately introduces secondary-phase precipitates. That arm is therefore at least partly outside the stated validity domain and adds a separate precipitation-strengthening mechanism.

The conditions claim that the comparison isolates lattice distortion, whereas introducing secondary phases or compositional gradients changes phase distribution and chemical heterogeneity in addition to disorder, so the proposed control does not isolate the named mediator.
